Some recovered destinations lack an unambiguous, exactly representable case/default relationship; their case values remain unknown. Unequal label and destination arrays are never paired by index.
Types and calling conventions are Ghidra decompiler observations, not source declarations.
Register variables, compiler-generated blocks, and pointer arithmetic remain decompiler artifacts.
Pseudocode is neither original source nor guaranteed to compile.

High p-code is decompiler-derived, not original source or runtime behavior. is_dead preserves the Java AST flag; decoded block members can retain that flag, so block_membership separately reports actual syntax-tree membership.
Def-use links do not cross function boundaries and may omit memory aliasing, call side effects, or unresolved indirect flow.

Memory read/write effects cover high-p-code LOAD and STORE operations only; direct memory address varnodes in other operations are not included. An empty effect list does not establish that no memory is accessed. Recorded instruction references may provide complementary evidence.
Memory read/write effects include stack and temporary memory operations; they do not identify persistent state or business meaning.
Operation, input, and def-use limits can truncate large functions; inspect the effective limits, limits_reached and omitted counts before drawing conclusions.
Known omitted-edge counts cover links omitted from retained operations; omitted operations may contain additional uncounted links.

ghidra.value_flow_max_operations reached its effective value of 3000. In MCP, use update_analysis_settings with setting ghidra.value_flow_max_operations, action set and a larger integer value from 1 to 2147483647, then repeat the selected function analysis on this Program without restarting REA. For a one-shot CLI retry, set REA_GHIDRA_VALUE_FLOW_MAX_OPERATIONS to a larger count in the environment that starts the next rea invocation, then repeat the selected analysis; the previous invocation's Program is no longer active. These controls do not raise the decompile deadline, bridge transport or MCP client limits.
Unresolved computed or indirect flows without target addresses are not represented as reference edges.
Thunk and external classifications are Ghidra FunctionManager observations; they do not resolve targetless calls.
Pseudocode and assembly are Ghidra-specific representations, not original source or Hopper-equivalent text.
Synthetic Ghidra entry-point references without actionable memory sources are omitted.
The session serves operations only after Ghidra reports default auto-analysis complete; incomplete analysis does not expose partial results.

Ghidra Program checkpoint mode is disabled: closing discards metadata edits; original executable bytes are unchanged. For stock ELF/PE/Mach-O on Linux/macOS, set REA_GHIDRA_CHECKPOINT_DIR to a private absolute directory before starting REA (restart MCP after changing its startup environment).
Cancelling an active Ghidra request terminates its ephemeral database and discards session annotations. The selected target remains open; the next provider query imports the original artifact again.
Default-space addresses use lowercase 0x-prefixed hexadecimal; other address spaces use <percent-encoded-space>:0x<hex>.
References cover the complete Ghidra function-body AddressSet and exact entry. Dossier incoming edges omit sources owned by that function; procedure_references also retains those internal edges.
The dossier combines Ghidra FunctionManager, Listing, ReferenceManager, BasicBlockModel, and decompiler observations; provider-specific pseudocode and assembly are not cross-provider text invariants.

Resolved reference metadata identifies computed, indirect, external, call, jump, and data edges; unresolved targetless flows remain unknown, and function classifications distinguish thunks and externals.
Synthetic Ghidra entry-point references without actionable memory sources are omitted.

The Java bridge serializes one function request per Program. Decompilation runs until completion or caller cancellation unless REA_GHIDRA_DECOMPILE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS sets a per-function limit. That limit stops the requested decompile without requesting session closure; caller cancellation requests session closure.

Windows Ghidra P0 accepts native x86, x86-64, ARMNT (Thumb-2) and ARM64 PE applications and DLLs, DOS MZ images, and explicitly selected raw 6502 images; managed, hostile, sensitive, and mutable-path targets are unsupported.
The Windows bridge uses authenticated IPv4 loopback because Node path-based IPC does not expose Java AF_UNIX sockets; the endpoint file contains no bearer token.

Windows sessions require the matching packaged Windows x64 native addon, local NTFS/ReFS targets and runtimes, and Windows 10 or later. Native handles enforce path admission, private DACLs, and Job Object ownership automatically.
